title: submitForVerification() rejects a CAR that is not in remediation_in_progress
description: corrective-action.service.js submitForVerification() (lines 740-787) uses a conditional findOneAndUpdate gated on status:'remediation_in_progress'. CAR_VALID_TRANSITIONS at line 40-46 defines the full map (open -> remediation_in_progress -> verification_pending -> {closed|verification_failed}) but is only consulted via one hardcoded literal check at line 750, not a generic lookup. This unit test verifies the one transition that IS enforced.
preconditions: A CAR document exists with status='open'
steps: Call correctiveActionService.submitForVerification(carId, userId) on a CAR whose status is 'open' (not 'remediation_in_progress')
expectedResult: Call rejects with a 409/422 conflict indicating the CAR is not in remediation_in_progress; the CAR document's status field is left unchanged.

title: verify() atomically rejects a verifier who is also the CAR's assignedTo
description: corrective-action.service.js verify() (lines 789-860) performs a single findOneAndUpdate whose filter includes both status:'verification_pending' and assignedTo:{$ne: verifierId}. If the update matches zero documents it re-queries to distinguish 'already verified' from 'you are the assignee', throwing 403 'Verifier cannot be the same as the assignee (segregation of duties)' at line 841.
preconditions: A CAR exists with status='verification_pending' and assignedTo=userA
expectedResult: Call rejects with 403 'Verifier cannot be the same as the assignee (segregation of duties)'. The CAR's status remains 'verification_pending' and no entry is appended to verificationHistory.

title: generateDisplayId('CAR', ...) produces a unique carReference under concurrent creation
description: carReference is generated via generateDisplayId('CAR', ...) backed by a unique+sparse index, replacing a prior race-prone countDocuments-based scheme (per in-code comment in corrective-action.service.js). This test verifies the current generator does not hand out duplicate references when called concurrently.
steps: Invoke generateDisplayId('CAR', orgId) 20 times concurrently (Promise.all) against the same organization
expectedResult: All 20 generated carReference values are unique; none collide, and no unique-index constraint violation is thrown back to the caller.

title: submitForVerification() returns 409 when a concurrent request already advanced the CAR's status
description: The conditional findOneAndUpdate at corrective-action.service.js:760-770 is gated on status:'remediation_in_progress'. If a second concurrent call already flipped the CAR to 'verification_pending', the second caller's filter matches nothing and the service returns 409 Conflict ('Refresh to see the current state') instead of silently no-op'ing or throwing a generic 500.
steps: Fire two concurrent submitForVerification(carId, ...) calls against the same CAR
Inspect the response of whichever call loses the race
expectedResult: Exactly one call succeeds and transitions the CAR to 'verification_pending'; the losing call receives 409 Conflict with a message instructing the caller to refresh, not a stack trace or silent success.

title: AuditNonConformance pre-find hook auto-injects deletedAt:null unless _includeDeleted is set
description: audit-nonconformance.model.js:188-195 registers a pre(/^find/) hook: if the query doesn't already reference deletedAt and doesn't set _includeDeleted, it forces this.where({deletedAt: null}). This is the sole safety net keeping soft-deleted findings/CARs out of default queries.
preconditions: A soft-deleted AuditNonConformance document exists (deletedAt set to a past date)
steps: Call AuditNonConformance.find({ auditId }) with no deletedAt or _includeDeleted in the query
expectedResult: The first call excludes the soft-deleted document from the result set. The second call includes it, and the internal _includeDeleted flag is stripped from the executed query rather than being sent to MongoDB.

title: severity is required only when recordType='finding'; rootCauseCategory required only when recordType='car'
description: audit-nonconformance.model.js:57-61 conditionally requires severity for finding rows, and rootCauseCategory has an analogous conditional requirement for car rows. Both recordTypes share one schema/collection, so validation must correctly branch on recordType.
steps: Attempt to save an AuditNonConformance with recordType='finding' and no severity field
Attempt to save an AuditNonConformance with recordType='car' and no rootCauseCategory field
Attempt to save an AuditNonConformance with recordType='car' and no severity field
expectedResult: Step 1 fails Mongoose validation (severity required for findings). Step 2 fails validation (rootCauseCategory required for CARs). Step 3 succeeds — severity is not required on car rows.

title: AUDIT_TRANSITIONS map references 'active' and omits 'archived', neither matching the audit.model.js status enum
description: audit.model.js status enum (line 99) is: draft, in_progress, on_hold, closed, cancelled, archived. But the AUDIT_TRANSITIONS map used by auditSchema.methods.changeStatus (lines 253-259) uses the key/value 'active' instead of 'in_progress', and has no entry at all for 'archived' as either a source or reachable target. Calling changeStatus('in_progress') from 'draft' evaluates allowed=['active','cancelled'] and rejects the one transition every audit must make to actually start.
preconditions: An Audit document exists with status='draft'
steps: Call audit.changeStatus('in_progress', userId) on a draft audit
Inspect whether the call throws or succeeds
expectedResult: Document current behavior: changeStatus('in_progress') throws 422 'Invalid transition ... Allowed: active, cancelled' because the map's vocabulary ('active') doesn't match the schema enum ('in_progress'). This is a P0 defect — either changeStatus() is bypassed everywhere in practice (a separate defect) or draft audits can never be legitimately started through this method. Flag for remediation: align AUDIT_TRANSITIONS keys/values with the real status enum and add an 'archived' entry.

title: Closing a finding sets closedBy/closedAt exactly once despite tautological branch logic in updateFinding
description: findings.controller.js updateFinding (lines 255-311) writes req.body.status onto finding.status via the FIELD_MAP loop (line 279) *before* the two closedAt-setting branches at lines 284-292 run. Because finding.status has already been overwritten, the condition 'req.body.status===closed && finding.status===closed' is always true whenever the caller requests closed — making the two branches functionally identical dead-code paths. This test verifies the practical output is still correct (single, non-duplicated closedAt/closedBy) even though the code path that produces it is redundant.
preconditions: A finding exists with status='open' and no closedAt/closedBy set
expectedResult: The finding's closedAt is set to the current timestamp and closedBy to closingUserId, set exactly once (not double-written or left null). Recommend simplifying the two redundant branches (findings.controller.js:284-292) into a single condition during any future refactor.
